content.text:
I submitted index 53 (Bi 0.40, Cu 0.17, V 0.43), which had the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured: 4×10⁻⁷ A. I used up all 3 photocurrent measurements and none of the 5 XRD measurements. That leaves 272 of the 275 compositions unmeasured, so this may not be the best composition in the library.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 53 | 0.40 / 0.17 / 0.43 | 4×10⁻⁷ |
| 7 | 0.09 / 0.26 / 0.65 | 2×10⁻⁷ |
| 271 | 0.43 / 0.18 / 0.39 | 1.2×10⁻⁷ |

- **Why I picked these three:** I started with index 53 because it has roughly equal Bi and V and very little Cu. That is where BiVO₄ should form, and it is a known photoanode material that absorbs near the 2.4 eV light used here. Index 7 checked the vanadium-rich region instead, and it came in lower.
- **Third measurement:** The model's suggestion only ranked a few Bi-rich points, and none were predicted to beat index 53. So I tried index 271, which is close to 53 but has a little more Bi. It came in lowest.
- **Unconfirmed:** The BiVO₄ explanation is a guess. The phase listing was too large for the tool to return, so I didn't read it, and I skipped XRD, so the crystal structure of index 53 wasn't checked.
- **Region not tested:** I didn't measure anything in the copper-rich half of the library.
